The '''Fulkerson–Chen–Anstee theorem''' is a result in [[graph theory]], a branch of [[combinatorics]]. It provides one of two known approaches solving the [[digraph realization problem]], i.e. it gives a necessary and sufficient condition for pairs of nonnegative [[integer]]s <math>((a_1,b_1),\ldots,(a_n,b_n))</math> to be the [[directed graph|indegree]]-[[directed graph|outdegree]] pairs of a [[directed graph|simple directed graph]]; a sequence obeying these conditions is called "digraphic". [[D. R. Fulkerson]]<ref name="Fulkerson">D.R. Fulkerson: ''Zero-one matrices with zero trace.'' In: ''Pacific J. Math.'' No. 12, 1960, pp. 831–836</ref> (1960) obtained a characterization analogous to the classical [[Erdős–Gallai theorem]] for graphs, but in contrast to this solution with exponentially many inequalities. In 1966 Chen <ref name="Chen">Wai-Kai Chen: ''On the realization of a (''p'',''s'')-digraph with prescribed degrees .'' In: ''Journal of the Franklin Institute'' No. 6, 1966, pp. 406–422</ref> improved this result in demanding the additional constraint that the integer pairs must be sorted in non-increasing [[Lexicographic order|lexicographical order]] leading to n inequalities. Anstee <ref name="Anstee">Richard Anstee: ''Properties of a class of (0,1)-matrices covering a given matrix.'' In: ''Can. J. Math.'', 1982, pp. 438–453</ref> (1982) observed in a different context that it is sufficient to have <math>a_1\geq\cdots\geq a_n</math>. Berger <ref name="Berger">Annabell Berger: ''A Note on the Characterization of Digraphic Sequences'' In: ''Discrete Mathematics'', 2014, pp. 38–41</ref> reinvented this result and gives a direct proof.

==Statement==
A sequence <math>((a_1,b_1 ),\ldots,(a_n,b_n))</math> of nonnegative integer pairs with <math>a_1\geq\cdots\geq a_n</math> is digraphic if and only if <math>\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i=\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_i</math> and the following inequality holds for ''k'' such that <math>1 \leq  k \leq n</math>:

: <math>
\sum^k_{i=1} a_i\leq \sum^k_{i=1} \min(b_i,k-1)+ \sum^n_{i=k+1} \min(b_i,k)
</math>

==Stronger versions==
Berger proved<ref name="Berger" /> that it suffices to consider the <math>k</math>th inequality such that <math>1 \leq k < n</math> with <math>a_k > a_{k+1}</math> and for <math>k = n</math>.

==Other notations==
The theorem can also be stated in terms of zero-one [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]]. The connection can be seen if one realizes that each [[directed graph]] has an [[adjacency matrix]] where the column sums and row sums correspond to <math>(a_1,\ldots,a_n)</math> and <math>(b_1,\ldots,b_n)</math>. Note that the diagonal of the matrix only contains zeros. There is a connection to the relation [[majorization]]. We define a sequence <math>(a^*_1,\ldots,a^*_n)</math> with <math>a^*_k:=|\{b_i|i>k, b_i \geq k\}| + |\{b_i|i \leq k, b_i \geq k-1\}|</math>. Sequence <math>(a^*_1,\ldots,a^*_n)</math> can also be determined by a [[corrected Ferrers diagram]]. Consider sequences <math>(a_1,\ldots,a_n)</math>, <math>(b_1,\ldots,b_n)</math> and <math>(a^*_1,\ldots,a^*_n)</math> as <math>n</math>-dimensional vectors <math>a</math>, <math>b</math> and <math>a^*</math>. Since <math>\sum_{i=1}^k a^*_i = \sum^k_{i=1} \min(b_i,k-1)+ \sum^n_{i=k+1} \min(b_i,k)</math> by applying the principle of [[double counting (proof technique)|double counting]], the theorem above states that a pair of nonnegative integer sequences <math>(a,b)</math> with nonincreasing <math>a</math> is digraphic [[if and only if]] vector <math>a^*</math> majorizes <math>a</math>.

==Generalization==
A sequence <math>((a_1,b_1 ),\ldots,(a_n,b_n))</math> of nonnegative integer pairs with <math>a_1\geq\cdots\geq a_n</math> is digraphic if and only if <math>\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i=\sum_{i=1}^{n}b_i</math> and there exists a sequence <math>c</math> such that the pair <math>(c,b)</math> is digraphic and <math>c</math> majorizes <math>a</math>.<ref name="Berger2">Annabell Berger: ''The connection between the number of realizations for degree sequences and majorization'' In: ''arXiv1212.5443'', 2012</ref>

==Characterizations for similar problems==
Similar theorems describe the degree sequences of simple graphs, simple directed graphs with loops, and simple bipartite graphs. The first problem is characterized by the [[Erdős–Gallai theorem]]. The latter two cases, which are equivalent see Berger,<ref name="Berger" /> are characterized by the [[Gale–Ryser theorem]].
